about: Simulated copies of a plastic bottle dropped at sea, moved by Drift's own drift model. Model output (a simulation with uncertainty), not observations and not a forecast.

model.name: Drift MLP drift model (public/model/drift.onnx)
model.architecture: MLP 10-128-128-4 SiLU, Gaussian NLL, standardisation baked in
model.trainedOn: NOAA GDP 6-hourly QC drifters 2012-01-01..2014-09-25, daily pairs; OSCAR monthly-climatology currents, QuikSCAT monthly-climatology winds

method: Drift's src/sim/ensemble.js run offline with the shipped ONNX model, as its Web Worker runs it: item "bottle", dropped on day of year 1, 24 members per drop, one day per step for 3650 days; each day a floating member moves by mu + sigma * z on the monthly OSCAR current and QuikSCAT wind climatology; beaching, resuspension, sinking and fragmentation follow src/sim/constants.js. A split clones a fragment's members, so branching copies share history. Per site, 40 of the copies alive at day 3650 were drawn uniformly with a fixed seed.

units.position: [lon, lat] in degrees, rounded to 0.1, lon in -180..180 (paths may wrap at the antimeridian)
units.time: samples[k] is the day since the drop (about one month apart)
units.state: one letter per sample: f floating, b beached, s sunk
units.trimming: p stops at the first sunk sample; a sunk copy never moves again, so hold its last position for the remaining samples

sites.name: Off Juan de Fuca Strait, British Columbia
Indian Ocean, south of Sri Lanka
